primary_topics: Toast delivered at the Diamond (60th) Wedding Anniversary celebration of Major Leonardo and Dr. Venus Santos -- parents of Monsignor Gerry Santos, CJP's beloved 'Anak,' May 7, 2017

The paradox of parents' grief at weddings: they think they lose a child but actually gain a son-in-law or daughter-in-law -- applied in reverse to Msgr. Gerry's priestly vocation (parents gained the Lord and the entire community)

Samuel Ullman's 'Youth' poem: the definition of staying young -- it is faith, not age, that determines youth; 'nobody grows old by merely living a number of years; people grow old only by deserting their ideals'
CJP's personal tribute to Monsignor Gerry Santos: as the Peter-figure who guided CJP's legal, business and judicial career in faith and morals
sub_topics: Wedding paradox opener: 'most parents grieve when their son or daughter marries, lamenting they are losing a son or a daughter. I always reply that they should instead rejoice because they are really gaining a son-in-law or a daughter-in-law'

The priestly vocation reversal: Msgr. Gerry's parents said 'No' when he wanted to be a priest; CJP would have given the same advice -- they should have rejoiced because instead of losing him to the Church they 'gained the Lord and the Christian community their illustrious son served'

The reason the Santos couple is still amazingly young, happy and good-looking after 60 years: Msgr. Gerry's homily noted how his father adored his mother, comparing her beauty to Joan Crawford and Paraluman; CJP: 'I do not know these movie stars, but I do know Marian Rivera, Kathleen Bernardo and Liza Soberano and the other current movie stars who are in the beauty league of Tita de Villa (who is with us today). In turn, all of them are as beautiful as Doctora Venus!'

Samuel Ullman's 'Youth' poem (quoted): 'Nobody grows old by merely living a number of years. People grow old only by deserting their ideals. The years may wrinkle the skin, but to give up interest wrinkles the soul... You are as young as your faith, as old as your doubt; as young as your self-confidence, as old as your fears, as young as your hope, as old as your despair. In the central place of your heart, there is a recording chamber; so long as it receives messages of beauty, hope, cheer and courage, so long are you young.'

Msgr. Gerry's role in CJP's life: 'whatever basic catechetical and theological knowledge I have, I owe to him who patiently taught this Catholic ignoramus... He has been my teacher of faith and morals in my stint as a justice and chief justice'

The Peter reference: 'since then he has been to me the Peter, spoken of in the First Reading during the Mass earlier today and the Shepherd extolled in the Gospel, throughout my legal, business and judicial career'

Toast: 'May we, who are aspiring to celebrate our 60 years of marriage, emulate them. And may the good Lord grant them another 60 years of marital bliss. And may they invite all of us again on that day 60 years from now.'

stances.claim: When a son becomes a priest, his parents do not lose a son -- they gain the Lord and the entire community he serves. Applied to the Santos couple: by saying 'No' to Msgr. Gerry's priestly vocation, they actually preserved him for a wider family -- 'you and me and all of us here in this ballroom numbering over 300 plus the countless parishioners, seminarians, students and other people he touched.' Their rejoicing at his priestly service is the reason they remain amazingly young at 60+ years of marriage.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered May 7, 2017 at the Diamond (60th) Wedding Anniversary celebration of Major Leonardo and Dr. Venus Santos -- parents of Monsignor Gerry Santos, CJP's beloved 'Anak' -- this toast by CJP opens with the wedding-paradox observation: most parents grieve at losing a child to marriage, but they should rejoice at gaining a son-in-law or daughter-in-law. Applied in reverse to Msgr. Gerry's priestly vocation: when his mother was 'the first to say No,' CJP says he would have given the same advice -- not to refuse, but to rejoice, because instead of losing Msgr. Gerry they 'gained the Lord and the Christian community their illustrious son served -- you and me and all of us here in this ballroom numbering over 300 plus the countless parishioners, seminarians, students and other people he touched.' That rejoicing, CJP argues, is 'the reason why after 60 years of marriage, they are still amazingly young, happy and good-looking.' He extends the beauty tribute through a generational arc: Msgr. Gerry's father compared Doctora Venus to Joan Crawford and Paraluman; CJP doesn't know those stars but knows Marian Rivera, Kathryn Bernardo and Liza Soberano -- 'in the beauty league of Tita de Villa (who is with us today); in turn, all of them are as beautiful as Doctora Venus!' He quotes Samuel Ullman's 'Youth' poem as his theoretical anchor: 'Nobody grows old by merely living a number of years. People grow old only by deserting their ideals... You are as young as your faith, as old as your doubt; as young as your self-confidence, as old as your fears.' He closes with a personal tribute to Msgr. Gerry -- 'since then he has been to me the Peter... and the Shepherd extolled in the Gospel, throughout my legal, business and judicial career. He has been my teacher of faith and morals in my stint as a justice and chief justice' -- and a toast to another 60 years of marital bliss.
